newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vetoes bill limiting environment powers.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vetoes bill limiting environment powers.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday vetoed a bill that would have stopped the government from invoking a rarely-used doctrine to protect fish and wildlife.

Clinton said in a statement he was against a bill that would have barred using "eminent domain" to protect portions of the Silvio O. Conte National Fish and Wildlife Refuge in New Hampshire and Vermont.
Under the doctrine of eminent domain, the government has the right to appropriate private property for public use, usually with compensation to the owner.
"This bill would undermine a constitutionally bestowed authority of the Federal government by prohibiting the use of eminent domain for fish and wildlife conservation," Clinton said in the statement.

The president argued that the federal Fish and Wildlife Service rarely used its right to eminent domain and that it had no intention of using it on the Conte refuge. But he said it was an important tool of last resort for the government.

Clinton said the refuge, which runs along the Connecticut River in Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Vermont, sought to restore the river's watershed chiefly through voluntary partnerships, cooperative agreements and environmental education.
Instead of the traditional approach of acquiring large tracts of land, he said the plan called for the government to acquire only 1200 acres (486 hectares) of land in New Hampshire and Vermont.
